priority.override_reason: The rank-1 recursive case is closed for this cycle by current exact frame-lifecycle profiles plus rejected contiguous-frame, boxed-frame, same-function-stack, local-pool, and compact-core experiments; the retained operand-stack pool already captures the non-regressing portion of that direction. The rank-2 hash-map profile attributes only about three percent of samples to the allocator even though each small object owns 384 bytes across ObjectRef and PropertyStorage, so property coallocation is a memory project rather than the highest current CPU return. Rank-3 string-tagcloud spends 949 of 3,411 current exact samples in PreparedRegexp::match_input, with repeated MatchState branching and allocation-heavy state-vector traversal. Copy-on-write capture snapshots remove a different shared allocation source without retrying rejected continuation, boundary-streaming, atom-metadata, or capture-free-program mechanisms.

mechanism.summary: Represent transient RegExp MatchState captures as an immutable reference-counted slice shared by branches and copied only when a capture slot is actually written, while keeping zero-capture states allocation-free and materializing the existing owned Vec only at the successful RegexpMatch boundary.
mechanism.generality: The representation applies to every matcher path solely from the pattern's capture count. PreparedRegexp owns one all-None seed; candidate starts, alternatives, lookarounds, repetitions, reverse matching, and duplicate-state keys share snapshots through ordinary MatchState cloning. A capture start, end, or clear uses copy-on-write isolation before mutation. There is no workload name, source path, pattern text, input size, iteration count, checksum, or expected-result condition, and no parser or observable RegExp protocol changes.
semantic_risks: preserving branch-local capture writes across alternatives, greedy and lazy repetition, lookaround, reverse matching, and backtracking
preserving capture clearing when a quantified group does not participate and preserving backreference reads from the correct snapshot
preserving content-based equality and hashing in duplicate-state suppression rather than comparing snapshot identity
keeping capture-free patterns allocation-free despite introducing the shared representation
converting the winning snapshot to the same ordered Vec of optional ranges at the RegexpMatch API boundary

profile_evidence.shared_cost: Of 3,411 main-thread samples, 949 are under PreparedRegexp::match_input. Its capture-bearing JSON-validation alternative repeatedly clones MatchState through match_pattern_first, repeat_atom, match_atom, lookaround-compatible branches, and duplicate-state keys; allocator and free entry points dominate the complete top-of-stack profile. The current owned Vec capture payload makes each branch snapshot an eager deep clone even when that branch never writes a capture.

profile_evidence.shared_cost: The independent input-validation workload places 252 of 2,621 samples in PreparedRegexp::match_input, including nested capture-bearing match_pattern_first and repeat_atom paths. This confirms the representation is shared, while the 9.61 percent whole-workload ceiling is too small to declare validate-input a ten-percent target, so it remains a regression control.
